messages:
Maria: Hey team — spike of Xid/ECC errors hitting eu-west-1 GPU pool since ~03:44. Noticed a few nodes flapping with the same kernel trace. Attaching dmesg/journal snippets I pulled. Can we agree on a minimal snippet schema we collect automatically so triage is faster?

Maria: dmesg excerpt:
```
[Thu Mar 12 03:44:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, PID: 8423, ThreadedFuncName
[Thu Mar 12 03:44:12] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

Maria: journalctl lines around that time:
```
Mar 12 03:44:11 node-123 kernel: NVRM: Xid 79 at 0x1f6b0e0 kernel: gpu watchdog timeout
Mar 12 03:44:12 node-123 systemd[1]: docker.service: main process exited with code=1
```

Chen: Ack. I ran nv-snapshot on two suspects and uploaded to the incident bucket. We need the collector to capture: node-id, kernel version, nvidia-driver version, pci ids, dmesg window (±5s), journalctl kernel messages (±10s), and nvidia-smi -q -x at the point of failure. Right now we only get last 1k of dmesg which misses early alloc errors.

Alex: +1. Suggest a compact snippet schema (fields, order) so our fast parser can correlate Xid codes -> driver versions -> GPU serials quickly. Minimal JSON fields: node, ts, xid, kernel, driver, gpu_index, pci_addr, nv-smi-xml, dmesg_tail.

Sam: Proposed grep/parse snippets we can add to loghook: 
```
# collect kernel and nv logs within +/-10s of event ts
EVENT_TS=\"${EVENT_TS}\"
journalctl -k --since "${EVENT_TS} -10s" --until "${EVENT_TS} +10s" --no-pager | grep -i --color=never -E "nvrm|xid|gpu" > /var/log/gpu-event-${NODE}-${EVENT_TS}.log
dmesg -T | grep -i -n -E "Xid|NVRM|GPU has fallen off" -A6 -B2 > /var/log/dmesg-gpu-${NODE}-${EVENT_TS}.log
nvidia-smi -q -x > /var/log/nvidia-smi-${NODE}-${EVENT_TS}.xml
```

Sam: Also one-liner to extract xid from dmesg for quick triage:
```
dmesg -T | grep -i Xid | tail -n 50 | perl -nE 'if(/Xid.*?(\d+)/){print "${1}\\n"}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr
```

Chen: If we standardize the file names and add a label in our telemetry envelope (eg. "gpu_event: true", "gpu_xid: 79"), the attribution pipeline can auto-attach snapshot artifacts to the node card. Right now it's a manual step.

Maria: Would be useful to include a short raw nvlink/PCI topology dump too (lspci -vvnn for the card) — sometimes swapped risers produce identical driver symptoms.

Alex: For immediate wins: 1) Expand loghook window to +/-10s for kernel logs, 2) add nvidia-smi -q -x snapshot on kernel Xid, 3) add GPU metadata labels to telemetry envelope. I can PR the parser to consume the new schema.

infra-bot: snapshot uploaded -> s3://redwood-telemetry/incidents/2026-03-12/node-123-nv-snapshot-1719254321.tgz :package:

Chen: Oncall follow-up: I'll run batch grep across eu-west pool for similar Xid codes and mark any node with >3 occurrences in 24h for replacement. Also will tag the snapshots with "suspected-hardware" if PCI/AER errors present.

Maria: Great. Can we add a tiny eval metric in console to show "gpu_event_rate" per pool? Would help product decide drain vs. speculative reboot.

Sam: Will implement the loghook changes and drop a deploy patch by EOD. Also adding the sample regex/one-liner to runbook.

Alex: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the short playbook for future triage. If anyone wants to test the parser run `python tools/gpu_parse.py --sample s3://...` and ping me. :thumbsup:
